findings.text: a seven-day clock that is measured but carries no reset stamp makes _instant raise ValueError and takes the whole week's report down with it, so that row is neither replayed nor reported unmeasured: WindowFigure.resets_at is typed str | None (reckon/crew/window_reading.py:56), _reset_text returns None for a window carrying no resetsAt (reckon/crew/window_reading.py:241-246) and budget._clock still emits state observed beside resets_at None for such a reading (reckon/budget.py:1764-1773), so one lane whose newest window event omits the reset stamp converts the entire replay into a traceback instead of an unmeasured row; reproduced by my probe at the reviewed head (review-unplaceable-clock.log), and absent from the 30 recorded pace rows I scanned, so it is latent rather than present in the recorded week.

item_verdicts.diff: Read the six commits the prior review covered and the repair d5d26a7b commit by commit: the repair adds the explicit unmeasured, unverifiable and unknown states at reckon/crew/pace_replay.py:31-32,103-167,269-284,332-343 and their regressions at tests/test_pace_replay.py:236-308, removing the prior head's None==None allowance match, its stored-held fallback and its metered default.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when asks for a synthesised week whose rows reproduce each allowance and hold by recomputation through reckon/crew/pace.py, the class split printed, a deliberately mistuned drain_lead_hours flagged, both measured files in one invocation with the base arm red and zero added failures, and a ruff delta; tests/test_pace_replay.py:236-308 now pins each repaired rule, my own one-invocation run of both measured files at the reviewed head in a scratch tree returned 15 passed EXIT=0 (review-head-gate.log), the repaired test file run against the prior module returned 3 failed EXIT=1 (review-regressions-prior-arm.log), and ruff check and format are clean on both changed files.
item_verdicts.goal: The goal asks that a week of committed pace rows replay into the pace curve, the local-versus-metered split by class of work and every hold decision with no stream read, and replaying the real committed week of 8 pace-bearing rows under docs/state/reckon/runs/ through reckon/crew/pace_replay.py:67-178 now prints "allowances: 0/8 reproduced (mismatch; 8 unmeasured)" where the prior head printed "allowances: 8/8 reproduced (ok)", with the split printed and no stream, receipt, live pointer or configuration layer opened (review-realweek-head.log, review-realweek-prior.log).
item_verdicts.manifest: The manifest at reports/reckon/s22-coord/pace-rows-replay-the-week/manifest.md carries status complete, the seven commits ending d5d26a7b, a 15-passed EXIT=0 gate at the reviewed head with the three regressions red at the prior head, and `reckon crew check-manifest --run r-20260926T204353115391-pace-rows-replay-the-week` returns ok true with no findings, with its negative_control_log's first line repeating the declared mutation verbatim.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The declared five paths are reckon/crew/pace_replay.py, tests/test_pace_replay.py, docs/evidence/archive/a-window-paces-the-lane-landed.html, docs/figures/a-window-paces-the-lane and docs/plans/a-window-paces-the-lane.html, and git diff --name-only 99455576..d5d26a7b lists exactly those five, the repair commit d5d26a7b adding only the two Python files inside them.

justifications.durability: Each repaired rule now has a regression that reddens when the guard is removed - my three mutations (unobserved clock back to None, the stored-held fallback, the metered default) each redden exactly one test in tests/test_pace_replay.py:236-308 with the module restored to md5 87b0815643bc0bb02bbb9fe8858236b0 after each (review-mutation-arm.log) - but the measured-without-reset shape at reckon/crew/pace_replay.py:244 has no behaviour and no guard, which the finding names.
justifications.evidence: The gate's two-arm result is recorded with revision, tree and command rather than claimed (final-measured.log: 15 passed EXIT=0 at d5d26a7b; review-regressions-base.log: the three regressions red at the prior module) and I re-derived both arms independently (review-head-gate.log: 15 passed EXIT=0 in one invocation; review-regressions-prior-arm.log: 3 failed EXIT=1), with the reviewed manifest's control first line matching its declared mutation verbatim.
justifications.fit: The repair follows the module's own idiom - module-level sentinels at reckon/crew/pace_replay.py:31-32, one explicit flag per evidence state in the per-row check beside parallel report counters - passes ruff check and format, and introduces no forbidden name, its only wart being the local name allowance_unmeasured reused as a boolean at reckon/crew/pace_replay.py:103 and a list of ids at :138.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The three prior findings are closed at this head - an unobserved clock counts in allowances.unmeasured and excludes itself from mismatches (reckon/crew/pace_replay.py:103-108,138-140), a hold without threshold evidence is unverifiable (reckon/crew/pace_replay.py:281-282) and an unnamed lane counts in the split's unknown column (reckon/crew/pace_replay.py:341-342) - and the committed week now replays to 0/8 reproduced with 8 unmeasured, leaving only the measured-without-reset clock shape that still raises at reckon/crew/pace_replay.py:244.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 99455576..d5d26a7b lists exactly the five declared paths, the repair touches only reckon/crew/pace_replay.py and tests/test_pace_replay.py, and the naming checks find no plan, sprint or stage token and no changelog prose in either measured file.
